purpose: Switch same-process importer public-shape consumption from dependency ModuleSymbols/body reads to the generated in-memory ModuleInterface while retaining the current body producer path.
question: When an imported module interface is available, which importer operations must consume it before dependency-body removal is attempted?
decision: After checkModule produces a target module's public export state, TypeChecker rebuilds the in-memory ModuleInterface and uses its values, structs, enums, and methods for direct imports, namespace imports, and re-exports. Snapshot-local resolved names and method receiver metadata are retained for current same-program lowering. ModuleSymbols remains the producer and local recording table.

consumer_matrix.direct_import: Read interface values, structs, enums, and methods; declare them in the importing module scope.
consumer_matrix.namespace_import: Read the same interface records, then apply existing namespace qualification and alias checks.
consumer_matrix.re_export: Select names and forward struct methods from the target interface, preserving duplicate and missing-export diagnostics.
consumer_matrix.producer: checkModule and ModuleSymbols still check dependency bodies and create the public export state before interface consumption.
consumer_matrix.lowering_identity: In-memory value resolvedName and method receiver/resolvedName metadata preserve current same-program lowering behavior; cross-build identities remain deferred.

compatibility_boundary.diagnostics: Existing import, duplicate, missing-export, namespace, and generic diagnostics retain their source tokens and messages.
compatibility_boundary.semantics: Import visibility, re-export behavior, type compatibility, IR, bytecode, cdbc text, runtime diagnostics, and Rust VM execution remain unchanged.
compatibility_boundary.separate_compilation: Dependency bodies are still checked in the same process to produce interfaces; this is not a serialized or independently compiled interface path.
compatibility_boundary.cycles: Existing loader cycle rejection and TypeChecker checked-module behavior remain unchanged.

migration: Populate complete in-memory interface metadata, consume it for direct/namespace/re-export public shapes, and run the existing import/generic/method parity corpus. M3B owns independent module results, cache keys, and dependency-body deletion; M4 owns serialized artifact compatibility if module products are emitted.
quantitative_gate: The full m0d-2026-07-22-r1 inventory validates 1,745 cases with zero unexplained differences, including import, namespace, re-export, generic, method, artifact, runtime, boundary, and malformed cases. Focused module-interface and source-metadata tests pass alongside all legacy and canonical commands.
old_path_deletion_condition: Delete dependency-body importer reads only after M3B independent module results and cache decisions exist, interface-derived public metadata covers all current export families, and current lowering identities have a reviewed replacement. Do not delete direct-entry compatibility adapters.
affected_consumers: TypeChecker direct and namespace import checking
ModuleSymbols producer and local export recording
out_of_scope: serialized interface files and version negotiation
cross-build symbol identities and linker names
independent module checking and incremental cache keys
changes to user-visible output or Rust VM behavior
